title: A vector bundle on a regular curve has a saturated line subbundle
statement: Let $X$ be an integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] regular Noetherian scheme of dimension one with generic point $\eta$ and function field $K=\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$ [def-sc-function-field]. Let $\mathcal E$ be a finite locally free $\mathcal O_X$-module of constant rank $r\ge1$. For every nonzero $s\in\mathcal E_\eta$, let $\mathcal L$ be the kernel of the composite $\mathcal E\to j_*\mathcal E_\eta\to j_*(\mathcal E_\eta/Ks)$, where $j:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ is the generic-point morphism. Then $\mathcal L$ is an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], its generic fibre is $Ks$, and $\mathcal E/\mathcal L$ is finite locally free of constant rank $r-1$; thus $0\to\mathcal L\to\mathcal E\to\mathcal E/\mathcal L\to0$ is exact.

source.place: Proof of (*), paragraph beginning 'Let r>=2. Choose 0 != s in E_eta'; argument using saturation in each DVR stalk

proof.text: The germ map from each stalk $\mathcal E_x$ to the generic fibre $\mathcal E_\eta$ is injective because $X$ is integral and $\mathcal E_x$ is free over the domain $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ ([lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field]). Therefore the stalk of the kernel is exactly $\mathcal L_x=\mathcal E_x\cap Ks$ inside $\mathcal E_\eta$, and the generic fibre of $\mathcal L$ is $Ks$.

source.place: Proof of (*), rank induction, sentence identifying the stalks of the kernel with E_x cap k(C)s

proof.text: At the generic point the local ring is the field $K$, and $\mathcal L_\eta=Ks$. At a non-generic point $x$, the chain $\eta<x$ and the dimension-one hypothesis give $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}=1$: a longer prime chain would give a longer specialization chain in $X$. Thus [lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr] makes $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ a DVR. Apply [lem-sc-dvr-saturation-line] to the free stalk $\mathcal E_x$ and nonzero $s$. It gives that $\mathcal L_x$ is free of rank one and $(\mathcal E/\mathcal L)_x$ is free of rank $r-1$.

source.place: Proof of (*), rank induction, local DVR calculation after the stalk identification

proof.text: The morphism $j:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated because its source has one point and $X$ is Noetherian; [pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh] makes $j_*(\mathcal E_\eta/Ks)$ quasi-coherent. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel] makes its kernel $\mathcal L$ quasi-coherent. Since $\mathcal E$ is coherent on the Noetherian $X$, [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth] makes $\mathcal L$ and $\mathcal E/\mathcal L$ coherent. Step 2 shows both have free stalks of the stated ranks, and [lem-sc-regular-curve-torsionfree-free] gives finite local freeness and constant rank. Thus $\mathcal L$ is invertible by [def-sc-invertible-module].

proof.text: The kernel inclusion and quotient map form a short exact sequence by the definitions of kernel and quotient. The generic-fibre description in Step 1 and the constant-rank conclusions in Step 3 give the asserted generic fibre, exact sequence, and ranks.
